title: RTTY and FSK
idea: RTTY shifts between two frequencies, mark and space, 170 Hz apart, sending 5-bit Baudot. Sent as audio tones on LSB, or by shifting the oscillator directly. Wrong sideband, swapped mark and space, or wrong baud and it won't decode.

rows: Data changes the oscillator's frequency directly
5-bit code plus start and stop bits
Reversed mark/space, wrong baud or wrong sideband: all of these

compare.how: Two audio tones into an SSB transmitter on LSB.
The data line shifts the oscillator's frequency itself.
5 bits plus start and stop; not 7-bit ASCII with parity.

traps.why: USB is the FT8 and data convention; RTTY via AFSK is LSB.
850 Hz is an old wide shift; amateur HF RTTY uses 170 Hz.

traps.wrong: A 7-bit code with start, stop, and parity bits
traps.why: That's ASCII-style framing. Baudot is 5 bits plus start and stop.
Dot and dash is Morse. FSK's two frequencies are mark and space.

traps.wrong: By keying an FM transmitter with a sub-audible tone
traps.why: Direct FSK changes the oscillator with the digital signal itself.
